books.section: C. President George Bush and the Persian Gulf War
The Presidency of George H. W. Bush

stem: Why did President Bush halt the ground war at the Iraqi border in February 1991 instead of advancing on Baghdad?

options.text: The coalition's mandate was limited to driving Iraq out of Kuwait
American forces had run out of fuel and ammunition
options.misconception: The ground offensive routed Iraq in days; no shortage stopped it.

options.text: The Soviet Union threatened to attack the United States if the war continued
options.misconception: The Soviet Union made no such threat; it was collapsing in 1991.

options.text: Congress voted to end the war before the ground offensive began
options.misconception: Congress authorized the use of force in January 1991; it did not vote to end the war.

rationales.A: Background: the coalition was unified around ejecting Iraq from Kuwait, not overthrowing Saddam Hussein, and the United Nations supported that limited mandate. Bush stopped at the border, leaving Saddam in power for years afterward.
rationales.B: The offensive was swift and decisive. Background: allied ground forces routed the Iraqi occupiers within days.
rationales.C: No Soviet threat existed in 1991. Background: the Soviet Union dissolved later that year.
rationales.D: Congress backed the war. Background: it authorized force in January 1991, before the air and ground offensives.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what the coalition had agreed to do, not what it could have done.
2. Background: the coalition was unified around ejecting Iraq from Kuwait, and the United Nations supported that limited mandate.
3. Overthrowing Saddam Hussein was not part of the agreement, and the Arab members of the coalition opposed it.
4. So Bush stopped at the border, and Saddam stayed in power for years afterward.
Remember: winning the war you declared is different from starting a new one.
